The proposed governing scale is a continuous brittle Al/Ti grain-boundary oxide, whereas the observed protective barrier is predominantly continuous Cr-rich Cr2O3, with Al/Ti oxides forming a discontinuous inner region.

explanation: The response addresses high-temperature environmental degradation and offers a testable atmosphere-switch experiment, but it does not reconstruct the study's principal intervention or mechanism. The relevant baseline was a dislocation-rich cellular single-fcc SLM state, not merely a homogeneous fcc alloy with unspecified grain-boundary segregation. Aging generated substantial L12 and L21 populations; Cr-depleted precipitates and added interfaces impaired early Cr2O3 establishment, causing consistently higher mass gain than in the as-printed state while leaving activation energies similar. The proposed Al/Ti-controlled brittle grain-boundary film conflicts with the observed continuous Cr-rich protective layer and discontinuous inner Al/Ti-rich oxide. Its 800–1000°C, minutes-to-hours domain also misses the documented 600–1200°C, up-to-96 h boundaries and the transition from subparabolic protection at lower temperatures to nearly parabolic oxide-thickness growth above roughly 900°C. Although microscopy plus mechanical testing could distinguish parts of the alternative hypothesis, no cited evidence supports the reducing-gas, void-coalescence, or catastrophic-failure claims.
